source.summary: GitHub Actions ‘Embedder footprint’ runs for PR #354 (branch fix/319-decoder-strictness at head 0bccf23bc6750a8e821872649841fb29125e62b2 — the #319 change (the component decoder enforces section sizes and core decode reasons are preserved) with the Codex-review follow-up (the InvalidSectionSize variant is classified as a decode error in the public ComponentError conversion), merged with current main 98e93a3d10354bee4a4a27e9b77252d69f066777 (PR #349); ubuntu-24.04, Rust 1.96.0): workflow_dispatch runs 45619016372, 45619023713 and 45619030678 against the branch and pull-request run 45619001703, which built the same tree, produced byte-identical sizes for every gated series
source.derivation: Second re-baseline for PR #354 (#319, the component decoder enforces section sizes and preserves core decode reasons), after PR #349 (#335) landed on main and the branch merged it (merge commit 0bccf23; the baseline files conflicted and were resolved by taking main's baseline as this campaign's base). The Codex-review follow-up on this PR (InvalidSectionSize classified as a decode error, commit 9bd4d1e) is part of the measured tree. Attribution was isolated by measuring current main alone three times (workflow_dispatch runs 45619036427, 45619042423 and 45619050607 on main at 98e93a3d10354bee4a4a27e9b77252d69f066777; all three runs pass the gate, and the main control is byte-identical to the checked-in baseline on all 32 gated series). This PR's own delta against the main control is identical in shape and size to its first re-baseline campaign: the four core configurations grow slightly in both profiles (release stripped file +304 B (core), +320 B (core-nosimd), +272 B (core-jit), +256 B (core-aot) and stripped .text +176/+176/+144/+144 B; release-size stripped file +512/+512/+416/+432 B and stripped .text +304/+320/+240/+240 B — the new WasmParserError::IntegerTooLarge variant and the format_io_error helper in the telomere library), and the three configurations that link telomere-component shrink substantially (release stripped file −123,976 B (component), −123,976 B (wasi), −123,992 B (wasi-threads) and stripped .text −112,064 B in each; release-size stripped file −69,160/−69,160/−69,128 B and stripped .text −63,232/−63,216/−63,184 B — every section body now parses through a take() size-limited reader, collapsing the generic section parsers to a single monomorphization). Following the established practice of re-baselining growth only, the sixteen core series are re-baselined to the branch measurements and the component-linking baselines are retained, so the retained baselines sit above the branch measurements by the shrinkage amounts above. Run-to-run spread was 0 B for every gated series across the four branch samples and across the three main samples. Against the original #164 baseline, the largest cumulative growth remains the release component stripped file series at +11.42% (2,433,656 B to 2,711,648 B), unchanged because that series' baseline is retained. The core-aot configuration, added by PR #267 after the #164 baseline, is not part of the cumulative comparison.
